increments.title: A correction round of pure coverage gaps runs test-author and reviewer only
increments.goal: Let the reviewer classify each finding it returns as a coverage gap or a defect, and have the workflow run a round whose findings are all coverage gaps through test-author and reviewer alone, visibly and on the record.
criteria: The reviewer's structured return carries a per-finding classification field that says whether the finding is a coverage gap or a defect; it is a value the reviewer sets, not a phrase the workflow greps out of prose.
When every finding of a round is classified a coverage gap, that correction round runs the test-author and the reviewer only, and does not run the researcher or the implementer.
A round with at least one finding classified a defect runs the full four-agent chain exactly as it does today.
The workflow log()s that it is correcting coverage only when it takes the shortened path.
The reviewer's classification of each finding is recorded in backlog.json alongside the round it belongs to.
The reviewer's own brief states what makes a finding a coverage gap rather than a defect, so the classification is decided the same way twice.
The test suite passes.

return.summary: Add tools/argus/scripts/with-collector.mjs, a fixture that starts a collector on a free port, runs one command against it and stops it whatever that command does, and name it in the shared agent brief and tools/argus/CLAUDE.md, guarded by a new node:test suite and five doc cases in test-repo.sh.
return.plan:
## What the tree actually holds, against the issue's account

Report these facts in the implement step's report; criterion 4 asks for them.

- The issue says no fixture starts and stops the collector for an agent. True: `tools/argus/scripts/` holds only `demo-emit.mjs`, and nothing anywhere starts a collector for ad-hoc use.
- The issue says `tools/argus/test/background.test.mjs` and `persist.test.mjs` already know how to start and stop one, unreachably. True and precise: `persist.test.mjs` line 111 has a private `startCollector({ cwd, args })` returning `{ base, port, proc, stop }`; `background.test.mjs` has `freePort()`, `runBackground()`, `collectorAnswers()` and `waitForSilence()`. Both are module-local in test files; neither is importable or runnable by an agent.
- What the issue does not say, and the change turns on: the collector already has the whole stop mechanism. `bin/argus.mjs start --exit-with <pid>` installs `exitWhenGone` (`src/background.mjs`), so a collector dies by itself when the process it was started from dies, and `--ready-fd 3` makes it announce `{ready, pid, port, endpoint, token, persist}` on fd 3. So the fixture is a thin wrapper over shipped mechanism, not a new lifecycle.
- `skills/argus/SKILL.md` line 29 and `tools/argus/README.md` line 45 both say "there is no stop command" — a true statement about the CLI, and the reason an agent that wanted a throwaway instance improvised a `pkill`.

## What gets built

### 1. `tools/argus/scripts/with-collector.mjs` (new, executable-by-node, ESM, zero dependencies)

Usage: `node tools/argus/scripts/with-collector.mjs [--port <n>] -- <command> [args...]`.

Behaviour, in order:

1. Parse arguments by hand: `--port <n>` (also `--port=<n>`), `--help`, and everything after the first bare `--` is the command. Do not reuse `parseArgs` from `src/config.mjs` — it has no notion of a `--` terminator and would swallow the command's own flags.
2. With no `--`, or with nothing after it, print the usage text on stderr and exit 2 without starting anything. `--help` prints the same usage on stdout and exits 0.
3. Choose the port: the given `--port`, or one the OS hands out by binding a `net` server to port 0 on 127.0.0.1 and closing it — the same trick the suites use. Never a hard-coded default.
4. Open a log file for the collector's own output at `path.join(os.tmpdir(), `argus-with-collector-${process.pid}.log`)` and pass its fd as the child's stdout and stderr, so a collector that fails to start leaves something to read.
5. Start the collector with `spawnBackground` imported from `../src/background.mjs`, argv `[<abs path to ../bin/argus.mjs>, 'start', '--port', String(port), '--no-persist', '--ready-fd', '3', '--exit-with', String(process.pid)]`. `--no-persist` is deliberate: ad-hoc inspection must leave no `.uroboros-telemetry` directory in whatever project the agent is standing in. `--exit-with <own pid>` is the backstop that makes the port free even when this wrapper is killed outright.
6. On rejection from `spawnBackground`, print one line on stderr naming the port, the log file and the error message, and exit 1 without running the command.
7. Print a banner on stderr — never stdout, so the command's stdout stays clean for an agent to parse — naming the endpoint, the pid as `pid <n>`, and that the collector stops when the command exits.
8. Run the command with `spawn(command, args, { stdio: 'inherit', env: { ...process.env, ARGUS_URL: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`, ARGUS_PORT: String(port) } })`, no shell.
9. Stop the collector in a `finally`, and from a `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handler: `process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM')`, poll `isRunning(pid)` (exported by `src/background.mjs`) every 50 ms for up to 5 s, then `SIGKILL` and poll for another 2 s, then confirm nothing accepts a connection on the port for up to 5 s.
10. Exit with the command's own exit code, or `128 + signal` when a signal killed it. If step 9 could not free the port, print a line naming the port and the pid and exit 70 instead, whatever the command returned — a leaked port is a failure of the fixture's one promise and must not be reported as success.

No `--token`, no `--persist`, no state file, no `stop` subcommand: the collector's design (`src/background.mjs`, and `background.test.mjs`'s "no pidfile, no stop command, no registry") is that a collector dies with the process it was started from, and a pidfile in a fixture would be a second, contradictory lifecycle. Rejected for that reason: a `start`/`stop` pair backed by a pidfile in the temp directory. Rejected as too little: exporting the test helper from a shared module, which leaves an agent writing Node to use it. Rejected as scope: an `argus stop` command in the CLI, which changes what the shipped tool promises and would need `skills/argus/SKILL.md`, `tools/argus/README.md` and `HELP` rewritten.

The child command gets `ARGUS_URL` and `ARGUS_PORT` and no other new variable. `UROBOROS_OBS_*` are the collector's configuration inputs; handing one back as an output would make the same name mean two things.

### 2. `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md`

Add one short section after "Reporting a command run" and before "Your step return", titled `## A live collector`. It must contain, in imperative sentences and once each:

- the literal command `node tools/argus/scripts/with-collector.mjs [--port <n>] -- <command>`;
- that it starts a collector on a free port, hands the command `ARGUS_URL` and `ARGUS_PORT`, and stops that collector when the command exits, whatever the command's exit code;
- that an agent must not start a collector by hand and must not kill one with `pkill`;
- that the script is there in an uroboros checkout — the plugin ships `skills/`, `workflows/` and `agents/` only (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`), so an agent working in another project has no `tools/argus/`.

Keep it to four sentences or fewer. Every agent pays for this page on every dispatch.

### 3. `tools/argus/CLAUDE.md`

Under "## Running it", add one line to the existing bash block:

```
node scripts/with-collector.mjs -- <cmd>   # a collector for one command, stopped when it exits
```

### 4. `test-repo.sh`

Append a new section immediately before the final `echo` and the `if [ "$failed" -eq 0 ]` summary block, with the five doc/asset cases the test plan specifies.

## Pages checked, and what was done with each

Criterion 3 asks for the sweep, so the implement report must carry this list. Checked for telling an agent how to reach a running collector: `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md` (said nothing — corrected), `tools/argus/CLAUDE.md` ("Running it" showed only the blocking `node bin/argus.mjs` — corrected), `README.md`, `tools/argus/README.md`, `skills/argus/SKILL.md`, `tools/argus-ui/README.md`, `tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md`, `rulebook.md`, `.claude/rules/agents.md`, all five `agents/*.md`, `skills/CLAUDE.md`, `skills/grill/SKILL.md`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md`, `workflows/loop.js`, `workflows/agile-loop.js`, `hooks/session-start.sh`, `bin/argus`.

Of those, `rulebook.md`, `.claude/rules/agents.md`, the five agent pages, `skills/grill/SKILL.md`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md`, `skills/CLAUDE.md`, both workflow scripts and `hooks/session-start.sh` never mention a collector at all — nothing to correct. `README.md`, `tools/argus/README.md`, `skills/argus/SKILL.md` and the two argus-ui pages document `argus start --background` for a session that is measuring itself; they are user-facing and ship through the plugin, so they must not gain a `tools/argus/scripts/…` path that does not exist outside a checkout, and their "there is no stop command" sentences stay true of the CLI. Leave all five untouched, and say so in the report rather than letting the omission read as an oversight. Do not repeat the instruction into the agent pages or the workflow prompts: the shared brief's own opening rule is that it carries what holds for every agent so a role page need not repeat it, and a second wording of one rule is what drifts.

## What the implement report has to state

- The tree-versus-issue account above.
- The page sweep above: every page checked, every page corrected, and why the five documented pages were left.
- That starting and stopping leaves no process holding the port, shown by a run you actually did. Beyond the checks, run this pair from the repository root and quote both exit codes:
  `node tools/argus/scripts/with-collector.mjs --port 4399 -- node -e "fetch(process.env.ARGUS_URL + '/api/health').then((r) => r.json()).then((b) => console.log(JSON.stringify(b)))"`
  then
  `node -e "const s = require('net').connect({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: 4399 }); s.on('connect', () => { console.log('HELD'); s.destroy(); process.exit(1); }); s.on('error', () => { console.log('free'); process.exit(0); });"`
  The second has to print `free` and exit 0.
- Each check command with its case count and exit code.
- Judge each criterion by whether the start-and-stop way exists and is documented, not by which file was edited.

Node >= 20.11 and bash are on the PATH; check with `node --version`. No install step: tools/argus has zero runtime and zero dev dependencies, `npm --prefix tools/argus test --silent` just runs `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"` and works with no node_modules present. There is no linter and no formatter in this repository. The tests bind loopback ports only and need no network. `node --test` runs the suite's files concurrently, so every case must take its port from the OS rather than hard-coding one. The argus suite is slow by construction — background.test.mjs sleeps for seconds at a time — so allow several minutes for it.

Commands used anywhere in this plan:

- `node --test tools/argus/test/with-collector.test.mjs` — only the new suite, from the repository root, for iterating.

return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. Two suites: a behavioural one for the fixture, and doc/asset cases in the repository suite so the brief cannot quietly stop naming it.

## A. tools/argus/test/with-collector.test.mjs (NEW, node:test, unit-level-integration)

Framework: `node:test` with `node:assert/strict`, ESM `.mjs`, no dependencies. Run just this file with `node --test tools/argus/test/with-collector.test.mjs` from the repository root.

Conventions to follow, taken from tools/argus/test/background.test.mjs — copy them, do not invent:
- Header imports: `import test from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert/strict';` then `node:fs`, `node:http`, `node:net`, `node:os`, `node:path`, `node:child_process`, `node:events`, `node:timers/promises` as `delay`, `node:util`'s `promisify`, `node:url`'s `fileURLToPath`.
- `const FIXTURE = fileURLToPath(new URL('../scripts/with-collector.mjs', import.meta.url));`
- Copy these helpers verbatim in shape: `projectDir()` (`fs.realpathSync(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'argus-project-')))`), `freePort()` (bind a `net` server to 0 on 127.0.0.1, read `address().port`, close), `collectorAnswers(port)` (fetch `/api/health`, `.ok`, false on throw), `waitForSilence(port, timeoutMs)` (poll `collectorAnswers` until false), `alive(pid)` (`process.kill(pid, 0)` in try/catch).
- Add one helper of your own, `nothingAccepts(port, timeoutMs)`: poll a raw `net.connect` on 127.0.0.1 until the connection is refused, returning true, or the deadline passes, returning false. A silent `/api/health` is weaker evidence than a refused connection, and the criterion is about the port being held.
- Run the fixture with `promisify(execFile)(process.execPath, [FIXTURE, ...args], { cwd, timeout: 60_000, encoding: 'utf8' })` and `.then(ok => ok, failure => failure)` where a non-zero exit is expected, exactly as `runBackground` and `secondStart` do there; read `result.code` for the exit code and `${result.stdout ?? ''}${result.stderr ?? ''}` for the output.
- Child commands are `.mjs` files written into the case's temp directory with `fs.writeFileSync` and run as `process.execPath <script>`, the way the `spawnBackground` cases write `child.mjs`.
- Test names are lowercase sentences describing the behaviour, not the function. Every `assert` carries a message saying why it matters.
- Every case cleans up in `finally`: `fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })`, close any server, kill any process it spawned, guarding `process.kill` with try/catch since a process that has already gone is not a failure.
- No case asserts a wall-clock duration; the per-command `timeout` is the only clock (tools/argus/CLAUDE.md).

The cases:

1. `a command run through the fixture reaches a live collector and leaves no measurement behind` — criterion 1. State: fresh `projectDir()` as cwd, no `--port`. Input: a child script that fetches `${process.env.ARGUS_URL}/api/health`, writes the parsed body to `out.json` in its cwd, and prints `process.env.ARGUS_PORT` on stdout. Expected: fixture exits 0; `out.json` parses and its `ok` is `true`; `result.stdout.trim()` equals that port and nothing else, proving the banner went to stderr; `.uroboros-telemetry` does not exist in the temp directory.

2. `the port is free and the collector gone once the fixture has returned` — criterion 2. State: `const port = await freePort()`, fresh cwd. Input: `--port <port> -- node <script that fetches /api/health once>`. Expected: exit 0; the pid parsed out of stderr with `/\bpid\b[^0-9]{0,12}(\d+)/i` is present, and `alive(pid)` is false (poll up to 5 s); `nothingAccepts(port, 10_000)` is true.

3. `a command that fails still takes the collector down, and its exit code comes back` — criterion 2, the exact failure the issue records. Input: a child script that fetches `/api/health` and then calls `process.exit(3)`. Expected: fixture exit code is 3; `nothingAccepts(port, 10_000)` is true; the banner's pid is not alive.

4. `two runs on the same port both get a collector` — the repeat edge. State: one `freePort()` used for both. Input: the same `--port <port> -- node <script writing a marker with the health body>` run twice in sequence, in two fresh cwds. Expected: both exit 0, both markers report `ok: true`, and `nothingAccepts(port, 10_000)` after the second. This is what goes red if the stop only silences the collector without releasing the socket.

5. `a fixture killed outright leaves no collector on the port` — the backstop, and the ugly path that produced the `pkill`. State: `freePort()`. Input: `spawn` (not `execFile`) the fixture with `--port <port> -- node -e "setTimeout(() => {}, 120000)"`, capturing stderr; wait until `collectorAnswers(port)` is true (poll to a 25 s deadline) and parse the pid from the stderr seen so far; then `wrapper.kill('SIGKILL')` and `await once(wrapper, 'exit')`. Expected: `nothingAccepts(port, 30_000)` is true — the 5 s `exitWhenGone` poll needs room — and the collector pid is not alive. Finally: kill the wrapper, the collector pid and any surviving child, each in try/catch.

6. `a port already held is reported, and the command never runs` — criterion 1's failure edge. State: an `http.createServer` squatter listening on `freePort()`; a fresh cwd. Input: `--port <port> -- node <script that writes marker.txt>`. Expected: exit code is non-zero; the combined output contains `String(port)`; `marker.txt` does not exist; the squatter is still listening afterwards (`collectorAnswers` is irrelevant here — assert the server object has not been closed by fetching it, or simply that `nothingAccepts` is false). Finally: close the squatter.

7. `with no command it says how it is used` — the empty edge. Input: the fixture with no arguments at all, and separately with `--port <freePort>` and no `--`. Expected: both exit with code 2 and print usage on stderr naming `--`; assert the output mentions `with-collector`. Nothing needs cleaning up.

Left untested, deliberately: the `--help` text and its wording; the exit-70 path for a teardown that could not free the port, which no case can provoke without breaking the collector on purpose; the location and contents of the collector's temp log file; whether the documentation prose reads well, which is the reviewer's to judge; two fixtures running at once, which the OS-assigned default port makes structural.

## B. test-repo.sh (EXISTING, bash)

Framework: plain bash with the file's own `ok "<why it passed>"` and `no "<why it failed>"` helpers and the `passed`/`failed` counters. Append one section immediately before the closing `echo` and the `if [ "$failed" -eq 0 ]` summary, opened exactly like its neighbours:

```
echo
echo "=== an agent has a documented way to start and stop a collector"
```

Put a comment above each case naming what it guards, the way the sections at lines 1269-1315 do, and print the offending lines with `| sed 's/^/       /'` in the `no` branch of a grep case. Run the whole file with `bash test-repo.sh` from the repository root.

The cases:

1. The shared brief names the fixture: `grep -qF 'tools/argus/scripts/with-collector.mjs' "$root/skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md"`. `-F` because the string carries slashes and dots. This is the case that goes red when the agent brief stops naming the way — the criterion says so in as many words.
2. The shared brief names the variable the fixture hands the command: `grep -qF 'ARGUS_URL' "$root/skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md"`, so an agent is told how to reach the collector and not only how to start it.
3. `tools/argus/CLAUDE.md` names it: `grep -qF 'scripts/with-collector.mjs' "$root/tools/argus/CLAUDE.md"`.
4. The script exists: `[ -f "$root/tools/argus/scripts/with-collector.mjs" ]`.
5. The script parses: `node --check "$root/tools/argus/scripts/with-collector.mjs" >/dev/null 2>&1` — the same pair the recorder gets at lines 321-330.

All five are positive assertions about what the pages say now, not the absence of an old phrase. No absence guard over `pkill`: the brief's own sentence tells agents not to use one, so a guard forbidding the word across the same file set would fail on the fix.

## What is already red

Nothing was run for this plan; no command was executed to produce it. Before the implementation lands, the new suite does not exist and the five bash cases are absent, so `npm --prefix tools/argus test --silent` and `bash test-repo.sh` are expected green on the current tree and go red only in the test-author's step, which is where the first run belongs.

## What counts as done

The two commands in `checks`, from the repository root, both exit 0. `npm --prefix tools/argus test --silent` covers the new suite together with the rest of the argus package, which also proves the new file coexists with the others under `node --test`'s concurrent file execution; running the file alone as well would buy nothing the package run does not. `./test.sh` as a whole is not in the list: the other suites are untouched by this increment, and the issue's "`./test.sh` is green" criterion is not one of mine.

increments.title: test.sh catches a commit-signing misconfiguration before an agent commits
increments.goal: Make ./test.sh verify that commit signing actually works in the environment it runs in, so a signing failure surfaces before an agent's first commit rather than after its work is done.
criteria: ./test.sh verifies that commit signing works in the environment it runs in - a signed commit in a throwaway repository, or the equivalent check the setup allows.
The check fails loudly and says what is misconfigured when signing does not work, and leaves nothing behind in the repository under test.

The check distinguishes an environment where signing is legitimately not configured for the run from one where signing is configured but fails, and does not make ./test.sh fail in the first; the report states which behaviour was chosen for each case and why.
./test.sh is green, and the report names the command, what it covered and its exit code.
increments.note: Sharpened the third criterion to name the two cases apart: the failure the issue evidences is a key configured and then ignored, which a naive is-signing-configured skip would pass over, and the criterion as written left that ambiguous.

increments.title: The loop skill pages tell the session how to tell a dead run from a live one
increments.goal: Correct the loop skill pages so the invoking session establishes liveness from the task's own status and knows that a user turn kills a running workflow.
criteria: The loop skill pages tell the invoking session to establish whether the run is alive from the task's own status, and say plainly that transcript file timestamps do not establish it.
The pages say that an ordinary user turn kills a running workflow, and that the killed agent restarts from zero rather than resuming mid-flight, so an interruption costs a whole agent.
The pages tell a session that takes a message mid-run to check liveness and resume rather than to report progress from stale files.
The pages do not describe the periodic self check-in or the resumeFromRunId re-entry, which another issue owns.
No loop skill page is left saying something the coverage-only correction round made false, such as an enumeration of the agents a correction round runs; the report names each page checked.

What the pages now say is provable: a check in the repository goes red when a page stops carrying the liveness rule or the user-turn fact, rather than the criteria resting on a reader's reading; the check is named with its case count.

This is the run's last pass over the loop pages, so it is also where a page left stale by the coverage-only change gets caught.
Closed done on this call: the review accepted it with no findings.

return.summary: Closed agent-affordances as done: the review accepted it at round 0 with no findings, record now reads fd 0 for a payload argument of `-` while the file-path form delegates to the unchanged reader, and the brief plus both workflows' recordStep() document the stdin form, pinned by seven node cases, two positive greps and a w20 driver mode (node --test backlog.test.mjs 23 cases exit 0; bash test-repo.sh 77 cases exit 0). Three increments stay open and four of at most eight are spent, so collector-fixture, signing-check and liveness-docs each still get a chain and the order stands: the two that touch the environment first, the pure-documentation one last. One change to the cut, and it is the only thing this increment taught that bears on the rest: agent-affordances found the record instruction living in four places at once - the shared brief, both workflow scripts, and five agent pages that defer to the brief verbatim - and its reviewer had to enumerate them to prove nothing stale was left. collector-fixture's third criterion said only that the agent brief names the way to start and stop a collector; it now also requires the report to name every page checked for where an agent is told how to reach a running collector, and every page corrected. liveness-docs already carries that sweep in its fifth criterion, so it is unchanged. Two things I deliberately did not turn into work. The reviewer noted the brief now documents a quoted heredoc while its rationale says no agent has to survive a heredoc, and that the heredoc truncates if a return ever contains a line that is exactly RETURN; the criterion the issue set - a summary with quotes or markup records correctly - is met, and both observations are outside the issue's acceptance criteria, so inventing an increment for them would be scope this run was not given. I also left the order alone: risk-first would put signing-check ahead of collector-fixture, but both depend on the environment in the same way and nothing this increment showed separates them, so the reorder would be churn a reader pays for.
